question: The sum of seven integers is \(-1.\) What is the maximum number of the seven integers that can be larger than \(13?\)
solution:
An integer larger than \(13\) must be at least \(14\). If all seven integers were larger than \(13\), their sum would be at least
\[
7\times14=98,
\]
which cannot equal \(-1\). Thus at most six can be larger than \(13\).

To show that six are possible, choose six integers equal to \(14\) and the seventh equal to \(-85\). Repeated values are allowed, and
\[
6\times14+(-85)=84-85=-1.
\]
Exactly six of these integers exceed \(13\), so the maximum is \(6\), choice D.

nodes.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. nodes.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers ; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram .

nodes.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation. nodes.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.
